title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 763B on Strata
summary: A 763B MoE at 2.00 bpw on a 12 GB card: dense weights and about 260 experts in VRAM, a 27 GB expert store in RAM, the rest read from NVMe. It runs, at about 5 tok/s decode.

model.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
model.architecture: MoE, 384 routed experts per layer, 6 active

weights.notes: Installed by Strata as model IST-DAS-2.00bpw; 257 GB on disk including the 111 GB Engram n-gram table.

hardware.notes: PCIe 4.0 x16. Needs about 260 GB of free NVMe and about 35 GB of free RAM.

serve.command: strata install -- --family deepseek41 --model IST-DAS-2.00bpw --data-dir <weights dir> --yes --no-start && ./run_variant.sh faster
key_flags: memory cap of 44 GB if your job runner counts page cache

placement: VRAM: dense weights (5.86 GB) and 252-262 of 15,360 routed experts. RAM: a store of about 2,600 hot experts (26-27 GB). NVMe: the other ~100 GB of experts read in place, and the 111 GB Engram table read a few rows per token.

caveats: A measurement report, not a tuned recipe: no llama.cpp baseline and no CPU-vs-NVMe separation yet.
About half of Strata's published 8-11 tok/s for a 3060 with 46 GB RAM.
Not for interactive coding: a short question waits 12-19 s for its first token.
Storage sets the speed. The same run from a hard disk decoded at 0.46 tok/s.
Full quality at an 8K prompt gave an unexplained slow result (1.99 tok/s) and is excluded.
